bands.label: Exemplar
bands.blurb: Reference-quality API operations across every facet.

providers.name: Klarna
providers.description: Klarna Bank AB is a Swedish licensed bank and payments network serving 150M+ consumers and 600k+ merchants with buy-now-pay-later, financing, cards, banking and a shopping app. For developers Klarna publishes a merchant API estate covering payment sessions and authorization (Klarna Payments), hosted checkout (Klarna Checkout and the Hosted Payment Page), post-purchase order management (capture, refund, cancel, extend due date), customer tokens for recurring purchases, settlement payouts and transaction reporting, the Merchant Card Service, and a PSD2 XS2A open-banking API for licensed TPPs. Authentication is HTTP Basic with a Klarna-issued API key; Sign in with Klarna adds a full OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect consumer-identity surface. Klarna publishes rate limits, a six-month deprecation policy, public service-level objectives, a self-serve playground with market-specific sample data, and an llms.txt — but no fetchable OpenAPI, no server-side SDK in any language, and no MCP server.

bands.label: Strong
bands.blurb: Solid contracts, transparent operations, and an easy start.

providers.name: Bokio
providers.description: Bokio is a Swedish cloud accounting and bookkeeping platform (a Visma company) for small businesses, sole traders and their accountants, combining automated bookkeeping, invoicing, a business bank account and financial reporting. Its public REST API is split into a Company API (journal entries, invoices, credit notes, customers, items, suppliers and supplier invoices, uploads, bank payments, chart of accounts, fiscal years and SIE export) and a General API that handles OAuth 2.0 token issuance and connection management for public multi-tenant integrations. Authentication is OAuth 2.0 (authorization code and client credentials) with 24 fine-grained resource:action scopes; the API uses URI-path versioning (v1), page-number pagination, per-token rate limits and a documented deprecation, brownout and sunset lifecycle.

providers.name: Northmill
providers.description: Northmill Bank AB is a Swedish technology-driven bank, founded in Stockholm in 2006 and licensed by Finansinspektionen in 2019, that serves roughly 600,000 private customers and 2,500 businesses across Sweden, Norway and Finland with savings accounts, cards, personal and business lending, business accounts, Swish and card acquiring. Through its Northmill Flo business unit (formerly MoreFlo, acquired and rebranded) it also ships point-of-sale, booking, checkout and e-commerce products for retail and hospitality merchants. Its public developer surface is the Flo API - a Swagger 2.0 REST contract published at api.moreflo.com with 199 operations over articles, stock, orders, receipts, customers, bookings, campaigns, vouchers, SMS and webhooks - alongside a PSD2 open-banking interface for third-party providers documented under the Northmill Bank brand and delivered on Token.io infrastructure.

providers.name: IFS
providers.description: IFS is a global enterprise software company providing cloud ERP, enterprise asset management, field service management, and enterprise service management platforms. APIs enable integration with IFS Cloud across manufacturing, energy, aerospace, defense, and service industries. IFS is headquartered in Linköping, Sweden with operations in over 90 countries.

bands.label: Developing
bands.blurb: Real signal across most facets with visible, nameable gaps.

providers.name: Telia Company
providers.description: Telia Company is the Nordic and Baltic telecommunications group headquartered in Solna, Sweden, operating mobile and fixed networks in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia, plus a global carrier and IoT business. As a mobile network operator it sits on the connectivity side of the telecom value chain rather than the developer-facing side, and its API posture reflects that split. Telia runs a real first-party developer hub at developer.teliacompany.io that fronts exactly two programmes — LSO Sonata (MEF/Mplify and TM Forum derived wholesale ordering APIs) and CAMARA (GSMA Open Gateway network APIs) — but both catalogs sit on Apigee portals that require an existing commercial agreement with Telia, a whitelisted corporate email domain and manual support approval before any specification or credential is issued. Only one OpenAPI definition is downloadable anonymously across the whole estate. Its CAMARA portal names Quality on Demand and Device Location but publishes nothing callable without login, and Telia reaches network-API developers mainly through Nokia's Network as Code aggregator platform rather than directly. The genuinely open surface is a public Bulk Messaging implementation guide covering an SMPP endpoint and an SMS REST API, and a gRPC audio-forwarding contract for its Telia ACE contact-centre product.

providers.name: Cambio Healthcare Systems
providers.description: Cambio Healthcare Systems is a Swedish health-IT company founded in 1993 in Linkoping and headquartered in Stockholm, best known for Cambio COSMIC, an electronic health record and clinical decision support platform used across Swedish regions, Denmark and the United Kingdom by well over 100,000 clinical users. Cambio runs a public developer programme, Cambio Open Services (COS), which publishes 19 REST APIs and an HL7 FHIR R4 server on Azure API Management at api.openservices.cambio.se, together with a published FHIR Implementation Guide of COSMIC-specific profiles, a Keycloak OpenID Connect authorization server with SMART-on-FHIR style scopes, and a synthetic-data sandbox. COSMIC and its clinical decision support are CE-marked and MDR-certified (notified body BSI-2797), and the company holds ISO 9001, 13485, 14001, 20000 and 27001 certifications.

providers.name: Uppsala University
providers.description: Uppsala University (Uppsala universitet) is Sweden's oldest university, founded in 1477, and a public research university ranked #103 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. It operates no central developer portal and no institution-wide open-data portal — data.uu.se, opendata.uu.se and api.uu.se do not resolve — so its programmable footprint is decentralized, sitting inside individual research infrastructures, the university library, and IT services. Four surfaces were verified live as institution-operated: the Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP) REST API at ucdpapi.pcr.uu.se, which is the university's most substantial public API and requires a free token; the Norse World REST-API at norseworld.nordiska.uu.se, returning JSON, GeoJSON and JSON-LD; the DiVA OAI-PMH endpoint at uu.diva-portal.org, notable because Uppsala University Library builds and hosts the DiVA platform for the whole Swedish DiVA consortium rather than renting it from a vendor; and the university's SWAMID-registered Shibboleth SAML 2.0 identity provider at weblogin.uu.se, which publishes machine-readable federation metadata. No Figshare, Elsevier Pure, Ex Libris or Dataverse contract is attributed to Uppsala in this profile.

providers.name: Safello
providers.description: Safello is a Swedish cryptocurrency brokerage founded in 2013, registered with the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finansinspektionen) and listed on Nasdaq First North Growth Market since 2021. It lets people buy, sell, trade, and store digital assets, and exposes a "Cryptocurrency as a Service" (CaaS) Institutional API so third-party organisations can embed crypto buying/selling, BankID customer onboarding, KYC and compliance verification, market data, order management, and wallet balances. The v2 Institutional API (base https://api.safello.com) uses OAuth2 with client-credentials, authorization-code, and a custom Swedish BankID grant, plus a staging environment at api.s4f3.io for testing.

providers.name: nordicmcp-eu
providers.description: NordicMCP provides Managed Cloud Proxy (MCP) endpoints tailored for AI assistants, delivering ready‑made integrations with services such as Weather, Google Mail, Fortnox, and Stripe. Users can quickly obtain unique endpoint URLs that include built‑in authentication, eliminating the need to manage individual API keys. The platform targets AI tools like Claude and Cursor, enabling seamless interaction with real‑world data through simple HTTP calls. NordicMCP aims to simplify AI‑assistant development by offering a centralized, secure gateway to multiple third‑party services.

providers.name: BankID
providers.description: BankID provides a digital identification and signing solution used widely across Sweden for secure online authentication and electronic signatures. It enables banks, government services, and private enterprises to verify user identities and authorize transactions through a mobile app and web integrations, supporting strong customer authentication and compliance with eIDAS standards. The platform offers APIs for developers to integrate BankID verification, signing, and user flow management into their applications, facilitating seamless and secure digital interactions.

providers.name: Lund University
providers.description: Lund University is a public research university in Lund, Sweden, founded in 1666, with roughly 46,000 students across nine faculties and the MAX IV and ESS research infrastructures on its doorstep. Its programmable footprint is narrow, real, and almost entirely library-operated: Lund University Libraries run two self-hosted publication repositories on the university's own host — Lund University Publications (LUP) for research output and LUP Student Papers for theses and degree projects — and each exposes the same open, keyless stack of a JSON(P) search API, an OAI-PMH 2.0 repository, an SRU 1.1/CQL search service, a unAPI 1 discovery service, RSS feeds and a bulk bibliographic export. Lund also operates its own Shibboleth Identity Provider, registered in the Swedish national federation SWAMID and interfederated through eduGAIN, which is a genuinely institution-operated machine-readable surface. Outside those, there is no central developer portal, no self-service API key, no open data portal at data.lu.se, and no public JSON endpoint behind the course finder — the education search at lunduniversity.lu.se is server-rendered with nothing machine-readable underneath. The research portal at portal.research.lu.se is the LUCRIS research information system running on Elsevier Pure: the data is Lund's, the contract is Elsevier's, and its web service refuses anonymous callers. Library discovery (LUBcat, LUBsearch) and the timetable (TimeEdit) are likewise vendor platforms carrying Lund's name.

providers.name: University of Gothenburg
providers.description: The University of Gothenburg (Göteborgs universitet) is a public research university in Sweden, founded in 1891, with roughly 37,000 students and 6,000 employees. Its programmable footprint is larger and more genuinely its own than the June 2026 profile of this repository recorded, and it is concentrated in one place: Språkbanken Text, the Swedish Language Bank's text division at the Department of Swedish, Multilingualism, Language Technology. Språkbanken publishes SIX OpenAPI documents from a single documentation index at ws.spraakbanken.gu.se/docs — Korp (corpus concordance search over 1,133 corpora), Karp v7 and Karp search v1 (lexical resources), Mink (upload, annotate and publish your own corpus), Sparv (the annotation pipeline as a job service) and the Språkbanken Text Metadata API (a 1,499-resource catalogue with BibTeX export). All six run on University of Gothenburg hosts, carry sb-info@svenska.gu.se as contact, and answered anonymous requests with HTTP 200 on 2026-09-01. The Gothenburg University Library separately operates GUPEA on DSpace 8.3, exposing both an OAI-PMH 2.0 harvesting endpoint (fourteen metadata formats, including the Swedish national uppsok thesis profile) and a HAL+JSON REST API on gupea.ub.gu.se. The University also runs its own Shibboleth SAML 2.0 identity provider, published as machine-readable metadata through SWAMID and eduGAIN. What is thin here is PRODUCT, not surface. There is no central developer portal, no API programme, no changelog, no status page, no rate-limit signal, no support channel and no documented credential-issuance route for any of the write surfaces. Five of the six contracts declare a security scheme and not one explains how to obtain a credential; two of them publish relative servers[] and no contact at all. This is a research unit's engineering that happens to be excellent, published without any of the institutional scaffolding that would make it findable. Everything else that looks like a University of Gothenburg API is a relationship rather than a contract — DOI registration with DataCite through the Swedish National Data Service and with Crossref directly, a Microsoft Entra tenancy on medarbetarportalen.gu.se — and those are recorded here with x-operator and no vendor contract stored.

providers.name: Telenor Sverige
providers.description: Telenor Sverige is the Swedish arm of the Telenor Group, a mobile, broadband and fixed-network operator serving consumers and businesses. Its developer portal at developer.telenor.se publishes OpenAPI contracts for corporate and partner integrations: mobile subscription ordering and administration, fixed-network quotation, product catalog, ordering and install base, product inventory, geographic sites, partner communication (user, catalog, CSTA, status), content charging and event notifications.

bands.label: Thin
bands.blurb: Limited machine-readable signal beyond documentation a human can read.

providers.name: Einride
providers.description: Einride is a Swedish freight technology company delivering an end-to-end platform for electric and autonomous road freight, combining purpose-built autonomous trucks, electric vehicles, smart charging, and the Saga operating software. Its developer-facing product, Einride Extend, exposes open, resource-oriented APIs (designed with Google AIP) over both gRPC and HTTP for booking truck tours and creating, releasing, and tracking shipments. The Extend APIs are alpha (v1beta1) and offered to select developers during an early-access phase, with a saga CLI, Buf Schema Registry proto module, and React UI component library. Einride serves customers including PepsiCo, Heineken, and DP World across Europe, the US, and the Middle East.

providers.name: Aduna
providers.description: Aduna is the Ericsson-led network API joint venture — a 50:50 company owned half by Ericsson (Stockholm, Sweden) and half by twelve global communications service providers including AT&T, Bharti Airtel, Deutsche Telekom, KDDI, Orange, Reliance Jio, Singtel, Telefonica, Telstra, T-Mobile, Verizon and Vodafone, with e& added later as an equity partner. Announced from Stockholm and incorporated as Aduna Global, LLC, it exists to aggregate CAMARA-standardised mobile network APIs from many carriers into one commercial channel so that developers do not have to negotiate operator by operator. Aduna sits in the exposure layer of the telecom value chain: it does not own spectrum and it does not sell to developers directly at scale — it aggregates operator capability and reaches the market through partner platforms (Google Cloud, Infobip, Sinch, Vonage, Microsoft Azure and the Azure Marketplace, Comviva on AWS, Bridge Alliance). Its API posture is honestly partner-gated. The public website documents an API catalogue in prose but publishes no OpenAPI, no sandbox and no self-serve signup; the developer documentation at docs.adunaglobal.com redirects every path to an Auth0 login wall at portal.adunaglobal.com, and the SDK onboarding instruction is to contact Aduna Global. The one genuinely open surface is a small set of source-available first-party SDK repositories on GitHub for CAMARA Number Verification v2, which are the only place Aduna's real endpoints, OAuth scopes and CIBA flow are publicly visible.

providers.name: Fyndiq
providers.description: Fyndiq is Sweden's largest online marketplace for bargains and deals, connecting merchants with millions of deal-seeking consumers across categories from electronics and mobile accessories to home, fashion, beauty and children's goods. Merchants list products while Fyndiq handles the storefront, customer relations and payments. Fyndiq exposes a REST Merchant API that lets sellers upload and manage product articles (create, bulk, price, quantity, delete) and retrieve, fulfil and cancel orders. The API is JSON over HTTPS, secured with HTTP Basic Authentication (Base64 merchantID:token), with a self-contained sandbox environment for integration testing and official Magento, PrestaShop and WooCommerce integration modules. Fyndiq is part of the CDON marketplace group and was originally backed by Northzone.

providers.name: Tradera
providers.description: Tradera is Sweden’s largest online marketplace for buying and selling second‑hand goods, ranging from collectibles and fashion to electronics and vehicles. The platform connects millions of users, offering a secure environment for auctions and direct sales, with features such as buyer protection, seller ratings, and integrated payment solutions. Tradera’s vibrant community fosters sustainable commerce by giving items a second life, supporting both hobbyists and everyday shoppers across a wide variety of categories.

providers.name: Airmee
providers.description: Airmee is a Stockholm-based last-mile delivery company (founded 2018 by Julian Lee and Adrian Prelipcean) that runs same-day and next-day home delivery, outdoor parcel-locker delivery and label-less returns for e-commerce retailers across Sweden — Amazon, Apotea, Adlibris, Acne Studios, Sellpy and Meds among them — on a proprietary Smart Logistics Platform that route-optimises deliveries in real time and reports 99%+ fossil-free transport. Retailers and transport-administration (TA) systems integrate through the Airmee Integration API on api.airmee.com, a JWT-authenticated REST surface that quotes delivery intervals for a zip code at checkout, checks service-area availability and parcel size thresholds, lists nearby collection points and parcel lockers, books home / locker / collection-point deliveries and returns, and cancels a booking before pickup. A first-party PHP SDK and Magento 2 module are on Packagist, and partner-built WooCommerce and Shopify connectors exist.

providers.name: compuute-se
providers.description: Compuute AB provides agentic AI security services, focusing on MCP server audits, vulnerability assessments, and compliance mapping for organizations deploying AI agents in regulated industries. Their offerings include static and manual code review of MCP server implementations, AI procurement risk audits, NIS2 & DORA compliance gap analysis, and an open‑source security scanner compuute‑scan. Based in Stockholm, Sweden, they target enterprise AI deployments with services such as prompt injection testing, tool poisoning analysis, and supply‑chain review. Contact: daniel@compuute.se.

providers.name: DBT Capital
providers.description: DBT Capital provides corporate loans to growing businesses in Sweden, offering financing from 5 to 150 million SEK for acquisitions, growth, refinancing, or working capital. The company emphasizes flexible loan terms and partners with the European Investment Fund (EIF) to guarantee financing, aiming to support companies throughout their development stages.

providers.name: Chalmers University of Technology
providers.description: Chalmers University of Technology (Chalmers tekniska hogskola) is a private technical university in Gothenburg, Sweden, run by the Chalmers Foundation and ranked in the QS World University Rankings. Unlike most of the university cohort, Chalmers operates a genuinely institution-owned API: the Chalmers Research API at api.research.chalmers.se, a first-party CRIS interface over research projects, organizations and publications, described by a live Swagger 2.0 document and protected by HTTP Basic authentication (public reads return 401). Around it sit two institution-hosted OAI-PMH endpoints — Chalmers Research (records back to 1942) and the Chalmers Open Digital Repository, a self-hosted DSpace 8.3 whose REST API answers on odr.chalmers.se — plus a SAML 2.0 identity provider registered in SWAMID, the Swedish national federation. Chalmers is a DataCite consortium member with its own repository account, and its CRIS carries ORCID iDs. There is no consolidated, self-service developer portal, no public open-data portal and no public course-catalog API; the teaching, timetable and data-deposit layers run on vendor tenancies (Canvas, TimeEdit, SND) whose contracts belong to those vendors, not to Chalmers.

providers.name: Eyevinn Technology
providers.description: Eyevinn Technology is a Stockholm, Sweden based video streaming consultancy and open source company specializing in cloud-native video infrastructure, HLS and MPEG-DASH packaging, FAST channels, WebRTC ingest (WHIP/WHEP), server-side ad insertion (SSAI), broadcast intercom, and player analytics. The company operates one of the largest video-focused open source portfolios on GitHub (300+ repositories across the Eyevinn and EyevinnOSC orgs) and runs Eyevinn Open Source Cloud (OSC), a managed multi-tenant SaaS platform that packages 180+ open source projects (databases, media tools, developer tools, AI runtimes, productivity apps) into one-click deployments with a token-based consumption model, a Personal Access Token (PAT) authenticated REST API, and client SDKs for TypeScript, Go, and Terraform. Eyevinn shares OSC revenue with the maintainers of the open source projects hosted on the platform, positioning OSC as a "Builder Economy" distribution channel for open source rather than a vendor-lock-in PaaS.

providers.name: Voi
providers.description: Voi Technology is a Swedish micromobility company founded in Stockholm in 2018 that operates shared e-scooters and e-bikes in more than 100 cities across Europe. Voi publishes a Mobility-as-a-Service partner surface for deep integrations (register users, start and end rentals, pricing, vehicles, and zone areas at partners.voiapp.io), plus MDS provider and flavored GBFS feeds for cities and mobility partners at mds.voiapp.io.

providers.name: Volvo Cars
providers.description: Volvo Cars is a Swedish premium automotive OEM (headquartered in Gothenburg, owned by Geely) that operates the Volvo Cars Developer Portal as the public face of its connected-vehicle platform. The portal exposes the Connected Vehicle API, Energy API, Energy Device API, and Location API for third-party developers to build applications around real Volvo cars equipped with Volvo On Call or Google Built-In. APIs use OAuth 2.0 against Volvo ID with explicit owner consent, a VCC-API-Key client identifier, and a free tier capped at 10,000 calls per day per app. The portal also covers Android Automotive in-car app development with an official XC40 Recharge emulator, 3D assets and simulator resources, and an active open-source program at github.com/volvo-cars.

providers.name: Fortnox
providers.description: Fortnox is a Swedish cloud accounting, ERP, and business-administration platform for small and medium-sized businesses and accounting bureaus. Its REST API at https://api.fortnox.se/3/ programmatically manages accounting and financial data - invoices, customers, articles, orders, offers, vouchers, accounts, suppliers, supplier invoices, projects, and financial years - authenticated with OAuth2 Authorization Code Flow. Fortnox also publishes a duplex WebSocket event stream at wss://ws.fortnox.se/topics-v1 that pushes minimal change notifications across domains so integrations can react to changes instead of polling.

providers.name: Kivra
providers.description: Kivra provides a digital mailbox service for individuals and businesses in Sweden, allowing users to receive, store, and manage electronic mail, invoices, and official documents securely. The platform aims to reduce paper usage and streamline communication between citizens, companies, and public authorities, offering features such as digital receipts, payment handling, and identity verification through Kivra ID.

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: 46elks
providers.description: 46elks is a Swedish communications platform as a service (CPaaS) offering a simple HTTP REST API for sending and receiving SMS and MMS, making and receiving voice calls with programmable call actions, provisioning virtual phone numbers, and handling media and recordings. The API uses HTTP Basic authentication with an API username and password, and is billed pay-as-you-go.

providers.name: KTH Royal Institute of Technology
providers.description: KTH Royal Institute of Technology (KTH) is Sweden's largest technical university, located in Stockholm. It offers a broad range of engineering and technology education, conducts cutting‑edge research, and collaborates with industry and international partners. KTH provides various digital services and APIs for students, researchers, and partners, supporting open data, learning platforms, and research infrastructure. The university is committed to sustainability, innovation, and societal impact through its extensive academic and research programs.

providers.name: Neko Health
providers.description: Neko Health is a Swedish preventive-healthcare company founded in 2018 by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. It designs, engineers, and assembles its own full-body scanning hardware in Stockholm and operates clinics across Sweden, the UK (London, Manchester, Birmingham) and, following a $700M Series C, the United States. The roughly 60-minute Neko Health Scan is a non-invasive, radiation-free examination that captures millions of data points across the skin, heart, blood, and circulation in a single visit, feeding a consumer patient app. Neko exposes no public third-party developer API; its only public machine surface is a Duende IdentityServer OIDC provider (account.nekohealth.com) that authenticates the patient application. This profile was surfaced as a venture-portfolio lead and enriched from Neko's public web and identity surface.

providers.name: Juni
providers.description: Juni is a Swedish fintech (headquartered in Göteborg, founded 2020) that provides a financial platform for ecommerce and digital businesses: business banking with multi-currency accounts, corporate and virtual cards, local and global payments, spend management, working-capital financing, and AI-driven accounting with integrations such as Fortnox. Juni is a licensed payment institution under the oversight of the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority (SFSA) and is backed by EQT Ventures. It exposes a regulatory PSD2 / Open Banking (ASPSP) API surface for third-party providers, but publishes no public product API, SDKs, or developer portal. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: KRY | LIVI
providers.description: KRY International AB is Europe's largest digital-first healthcare provider, founded in Stockholm in 2015 by Johannes Schildt. It delivers primary and specialist care through a mobile and web app — video and chat consultations with doctors, nurses, psychologists and physiotherapists — combined with a network of physical clinics. The company trades as KRY in Sweden, Norway and Germany and as Livi in the United Kingdom and France, and reports more than 14 million patient appointments, 4,000+ healthcare professionals and 60+ clinics. Alongside consumer care it sells digital clinical capacity to public payers (including the NHS and Swedish regions), employers, insurers and Employee Assistance Programmes. KRY publishes no public developer portal, API reference or SDKs; its consumer and partner surfaces are app- and contract-based, and patient authentication in Sweden runs on BankID.

providers.name: mypinpal-com
providers.description: Pinpal, built by Portfoliobox Stockholm AB, offers simple AI‑enabled note‑taking, project, and to‑do apps hosted in the EU. Founded in 2012 in Stockholm, the company serves about 30,000 paying customers, emphasizing privacy, plain‑Markdown data, and no AI training on user content.

providers.name: Försäkringskassan
providers.description: Försäkringskassan is Sweden’s national social insurance agency responsible for administering health insurance, parental benefits, pensions, and other welfare services. It provides digital services and APIs for citizens and businesses to access information, submit applications, and retrieve status updates. The agency focuses on secure, reliable, and user-friendly digital interactions, supporting a wide range of social security processes across the country.

providers.name: Lassie
providers.description: Lassie is a Swedish insurtech that sells preventive digital pet insurance for dogs and cats. Founded in Stockholm in 2020, the company pairs veterinary-care cover with an app-based prevention programme: owners take courses designed by animal experts and earn up to SEK 500 a year off their premium. Cover includes unlimited digital vet consultations through FirstVet, 24-hour claims handling, direct settlement with clinics, no breed or age restrictions and no lock-in period. Lassie AB is an insurance intermediary supervised by Finansinspektionen under the Swedish Insurance Distribution Act (2018:1219); policies are underwritten by Dina Forsakring AB. The company operates in Sweden, Germany and France with 100+ staff and more than one million insured animals, and is backed by a16z and Balderton Capital. Lassie publishes no public developer API - its GraphQL backend at api.lassie.co is private to its own apps - but it does publish a per-market llms.txt, making it an early example of a consumer insurer building an agent-readable surface without an API programme.

providers.name: novusmcp-se
providers.description: Novus MCP connects Fortnox accounting software with AI assistants like ChatGPT and Claude, enabling businesses to query their bookkeeping data via conversational interfaces. Operated by AMR Intelligence Sweden AB, the service emphasizes secure data handling, GDPR compliance, and flexible AI integration, offering a 30‑day open‑return policy and agency‑level support for agencies and enterprises.

providers.name: Bolagsverket
providers.description: Bolagsverket is Sweden’s official register of companies, providing public access to corporate information, filings, and open data APIs. It enables businesses, authorities, and developers to retrieve and submit company data such as registration details, annual reports, and ownership information. The agency supports digital services for company formation, changes, and compliance, offering both free and fee‑based APIs, downloadable datasets, and XML feeds for integration into external systems.

providers.name: Billecta
providers.description: Billecta provides a cloud‑based invoicing and payment automation platform for businesses in Sweden and beyond. Their solution automates the full invoicing flow, from invoice creation and delivery to payment collection and bookkeeping. Features include automated reminders, credit‑control, integration with accounting systems, and support for direct payments and auto‑giro. The service is offered as a SaaS product with a free trial and is designed for companies of all sizes, from startups to large enterprises. Billecta emphasizes ease of use, speed, and compliance with Swedish financial regulations.

providers.name: Trafikverket
providers.description: Trafikverket, the Swedish Transport Administration, is a government agency responsible for the long-term planning, construction, operation and maintenance of the nation’s road and railway infrastructure. It oversees traffic safety, vehicle registration, and provides extensive data services related to traffic flow, road conditions, public transport schedules, and infrastructure projects. The agency works to ensure efficient, safe, and sustainable transport across Sweden, offering APIs for developers to access real-time traffic information, road work updates, and transport statistics.

providers.name: Arbetsförmedlingen
providers.description: Arbetsförmedlingen is Sweden’s public employment service, offering job seekers access to job listings, career guidance, and support programs, while providing employers tools for recruitment and labor market analytics. The agency operates a comprehensive digital platform (arbetsformedlingen.se) with multilingual support, extensive statistics, and services for municipalities and partners, aiming to improve employment outcomes across the country.

providers.name: Stockholm University
providers.description: Stockholm University (Stockholms universitet) is a public research university in Sweden and one of the country's largest, with roughly 33,000 students across four faculties. It operates no public developer portal, no API gateway and no first-party documented API: api.su.se, data.su.se and developer.su.se do not resolve, and www.su.se/api returns 404. What the institution genuinely runs and serves anonymously is narrow — a Shibboleth SAML2 identity provider at idp.it.su.se whose entity metadata is published by the university and registered in the SWAMID federation (and so in eduGAIN), the Bolin Centre Database research data repository on bolin.su.se minting its own DataCite DOIs under prefix 10.17043 since 2014, and a SiteVision REST sitemap on www.su.se that indexes every course syllabus in the education archive. Its two harvestable research surfaces are both tenancies rather than SU engineering: the DiVA OAI-PMH endpoint at su.diva-portal.org is operated by the DiVA consortium at Uppsala University Library, and su.figshare.com is a Figshare deployment. This profile previously credited Stockholm University with eleven APIs that were all one Figshare contract at api.figshare.com/v2; those contracts and everything derived from them have been removed and the two repository relationships recorded as tenant surfaces instead.

providers.name: Rocker
providers.description: Rocker is a Swedish fintech company offering a peer‑to‑peer marketplace for buying and selling second‑hand goods, backed by a robust payment solution. The platform provides users with secure transactions, real‑time updates, and integrated banking features such as savings accounts and personal loans. Rocker aims to improve financial health by simplifying payments and offering tools for budgeting and financial planning, serving over 400 000 users across Scandinavia.

providers.name: FirstVet
providers.description: FirstVet is a digital veterinary care company offering 24/7 online video consultations with licensed veterinarians for dogs, cats, and other pets. Founded in Sweden, FirstVet operates a consumer telehealth platform across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States, providing virtual vet appointments, healthy pet checkups, follow-up care, and triage guidance on whether a case needs an in-clinic referral. The company partners with pet insurers and employers to offer covered or subsidized access to its subscription-based virtual care. FirstVet is a portfolio company of Creandum. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; FirstVet publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Lysa
providers.description: Lysa is a Swedish fintech company offering automated investment and savings services. It provides a digital platform where users can open accounts, invest in diversified portfolios, and benefit from automatic rebalancing and tax optimization. The service emphasizes low fees, transparency, and a user-friendly experience, aiming to make investing accessible to a broad audience. Lysa also offers pension transfers, savings accounts, and financial education resources.

providers.name: Nmbrs
providers.description: Nmbrs (Visma Nmbrs) is cloud HR and payroll software for the Netherlands and Sweden, widely used by employers, accountants, and payroll service providers. Nmbrs exposes its HRIS and payroll data through a public API in two generations. The current, forward-looking interface is a REST API served from https://api.nmbrsapp.com, authenticated with OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code flow via identityservice.nmbrs.com) plus a per-product subscription key, with granular scopes over companies, employees, employments, salaries, wage components, payruns, and absences. The older SOAP API (api.nmbrs.nl/soap/v3 - EmployeeService, CompanyService, DebtorService) remains available for existing integrations but is deprecated and scheduled to be retired on 1 March 2027, after which REST is the only supported API.

providers.name: Tobii
providers.description: Tobii is the global leader in eye tracking and attention computing, headquartered in Danderyd, Sweden and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Its developer offering centers on the Tobii Pro SDK — Python (tobii-research), .NET, C and Matlab bindings for streaming gaze and eye-tracking data from Tobii's screen-based and wearable eye trackers — together with the Tobii Pro Glasses 3 API (with official g3pylib Python and .NET client SDKs) and XR / consumer game-integration developer kits. Tobii's technology serves scientific and behavioral research, UX, healthcare, XR/VR, automotive driver monitoring and PC gaming markets.

providers.name: Blocket
providers.description: Blocket is Sweden’s largest online marketplace for buying and selling new and used items, ranging from cars, furniture, electronics, to real estate and services. It connects millions of users across the country, offering a platform for classifieds, auctions, and business listings. The site provides search, messaging, and secure transaction features, serving both private individuals and companies.

providers.name: Hormona
providers.description: Hormona is a women's hormonal-health company founded in 2020 by Karolina Lofqvist and Jasmine Tagesson, with offices in London, UK and Stockholm, Sweden. It builds a hormone-tracking mobile app together with an at-home hormone monitor and urine-test kits that users scan with a phone camera to get real-time, quantitative hormone results without a lab visit. The app uses AI to learn each user's patterns and predict when PMS or period symptoms are likely, offering 30+ tools to manage hormonal symptoms and supporting women from their first period through perimenopause and menopause. Hormona is distributed on the App Store and Google Play and is used by women in 185+ countries. It is a direct-to-consumer product with no public developer API program.

providers.name: Fishbrain
providers.description: Fishbrain is a Stockholm-based consumer technology company behind the largest social network and mobile app for recreational anglers, with a community of around 20 million fishermen and roughly 14 million logged catch locations. The app blends a social feed, a digital catch logbook with AI-powered species recognition, depth charts (from Garmin), local fishing reports with weather and bait intelligence, an AI-driven fishing-spot prediction map, and a searchable database of fishing regulations covering seasons, bag limits, and size rules. Fishbrain monetizes through a Fishbrain Pro subscription and is backed by Northzone and Seedcamp. It exposes no public developer API — api.fishbrain.com is a private backend for the iOS/Android apps — so this profile captures the company's public security, engineering, and web surface rather than an API.

providers.name: BioGaia
providers.description: BioGaia is a Swedish healthcare company specializing in probiotic research and products. It develops clinically studied probiotic strains for infants, children, and adults, focusing on gut health, immunity, and oral health. The company operates globally, offering products through retail and healthcare professional channels, and provides scientific resources and information on its website.

providers.name: Werlabs
providers.description: Werlabs AB is a Swedish health technology company offering preventive health check‑ups and laboratory testing services. Founded in 2013, Werlabs provides a digital platform where individuals can book comprehensive health examinations, receive personalized results, and access medical advice. The service covers women’s health, men’s health, blood tests, imaging, and chronic‑disease monitoring, partnering with accredited labs such as Synlab, Unilabs, and Karolinska University Laboratory. Werlabs is a registered health care provider with IVO and serves over 445 000 customers across Sweden.

providers.name: Kundo
providers.description: Kundo provides a comprehensive AI‑enhanced customer service platform that combines ticketing, knowledge management, and self‑service tools into a single SaaS solution. Built for enterprises, Kundo leverages artificial intelligence to keep knowledge bases up‑to‑date, automatically suggest answers, and streamline multi‑channel support. The platform offers AI Forms, AI Chat, and a knowledge agent that learns from existing content, helping support teams respond faster and improve customer satisfaction across various industries.

providers.name: Linas Matkasse
providers.description: Linas Matkasse is a Swedish meal-kit subscription service that delivers pre-portioned ingredients and nutritionally calculated recipes to customers' homes each week. Customers pick from more than 150 weekly recipes across concepts such as Chef's Choice, Family Favorites, Quick & Easy, Calorie-Smart, Vegetarian, Gluten-Free and Lactose-Free, and can change their selection until Tuesday night before a Saturday-to-Monday delivery. The brand is operated by Cheffelo, a Scandinavian meal-kit group listed on Nasdaq First North Growth Market that also runs Godtlevert in Norway and RetNemt in Denmark and delivers roughly 17 million meals a year. Linas Matkasse runs a consumer subscription e-commerce storefront and a "Mina Sidor" customer account area; it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Opti
providers.description: Opti is a Swedish fintech company offering digital savings and investment solutions. It provides a platform for personal and corporate customers to manage portfolios, pension funds, and sustainable investments. The service emphasizes transparent fees, automated savings, and a user-friendly interface, aiming to improve financial wellbeing through technology and data-driven insights.

providers.name: Bokadirekt
providers.description: Bokadirekt is a Swedish online platform that connects customers with beauty and wellness service providers such as massage therapists, naprapaths, hairdressers and more. Users can search for nearby professionals, view availability, and book appointments directly through the website. The service aims to simplify finding and scheduling personal care treatments, offering a convenient digital marketplace for both clients and service providers across Sweden.

providers.name: SMHI
providers.description: SMHI (Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute) is Sweden’s national authority for weather, water and climate information. It provides public services, research, and professional solutions, offering open data, forecasts, climate scenarios, and expert advice to support societal planning, safety, and sustainability. The institute gathers extensive observational data and develops models to inform the public, businesses, and policymakers about weather events, climate change, and water resources.

providers.name: Mindler
providers.description: Mindler provides online psychological counseling and mental health services through a digital platform. Users can book video sessions with licensed psychologists, access self‑help programs, and receive personalized treatment plans. The service operates across Sweden and offers multilingual support, aiming to make mental health care accessible and affordable.

providers.name: Matsmart
providers.description: Matsmart (operating internationally as Motatos) is a Swedish e-commerce company that fights food waste by selling surplus, short-dated, and overstocked groceries and household goods at a discount, with average savings of up to 50%. Its catalog spans pantry staples, beverages, snacks, candy, baby food, health and beauty, cleaning supplies, pet food, and non-food surplus, sourced from manufacturers and retailers and shipped across Sweden and other European markets via partners including Bring, Airmee, and PostNord. The company runs a consumer web storefront and iOS/Android apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network; it publishes no public developer API or documentation, so this profile captures its public web, security, and identity surface.

providers.name: Natural Cycles
providers.description: Natural Cycles is a Swedish women's-health company behind the first birth-control application cleared by the US FDA (2018) and CE-marked in Europe as a Class IIb medical device. Its subscription app uses a proprietary temperature-based algorithm to identify fertile and non-fertile days from a user's daily basal body temperature, supporting both preventing and planning pregnancy as well as cycle, ovulation, and perimenopause tracking. Temperature is captured with a paired Bluetooth basal thermometer or through consumer wearables the app integrates with — Apple Watch, Oura Ring, and the NC B1 band. Natural Cycles publishes clinical research, an educational content library (CycleMatters), an e-commerce shop for thermometers and tests, and a public bug-bounty / responsible-disclosure program, but it does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. Backed by EQT Ventures.

providers.name: Buildcheck
providers.description: Buildcheck is a Sweden-based cloud software platform that simplifies self-inspections and quality checklists for construction and infrastructure projects. The service uses AI to automatically generate project-specific inspection and control plans from uploaded building documents, then lets field teams document work on a mobile app with photo capture and digital signatures, share progress with clients through shareable links, and export organized PDF reports. It offers company-branded templates, role-based access, SSO and other enterprise features. Buildcheck was founded by Anders Jacobson (previously Next One Technology) and Johnny Wulcan (founder of Byggplanen). It is surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API or API documentation has been found on its site as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: SCB Statistics Sweden
providers.description: SCB Statistics Sweden is Sweden’s official statistical agency, providing comprehensive data on the country’s demographics, economy, labor market, and more. It offers public access to a wide range of statistical datasets and APIs for developers to integrate official statistics into applications, research, and analysis. The agency ensures high-quality, up-to-date information for policymakers, businesses, and the public.

providers.name: Clingsystems
providers.description: Clingsystems (Cling Systems AB) brokers surplus and end‑of‑life batteries, helping owners sell them to buyers while handling compliance, waste classification and cross‑border shipping. Their mission is to accelerate circular battery value chains, offering a marketplace, inventory visibility and transparent pricing to unlock value that would otherwise be lost.

providers.name: Min Doktor
providers.description: Min Doktor is a Swedish digital healthcare provider (operated by MD International AB) offering online primary care through its mobile app and web service. Founded in 2013 as one of Sweden's first digital-first care providers, it connects patients with doctors, psychologists and nurses for consultations, prescriptions, referrals and vaccinations, and also runs white-label care services for partners such as Skandia. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of EQT Ventures. Min Doktor operates as a consumer/patient-facing service and does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface; this profile captures its verifiable public security, identity and compliance footprint.

providers.name: Naturvårdsverket
providers.description: Naturvårdsverket is Sweden’s Environmental Protection Agency, working to promote a sustainable environment, climate transition, circular economy and biodiversity. It provides guidance, grants, data and statistics, and supports stakeholders through policies, regulations and tools aimed at improving environmental quality across the nation.

providers.name: Saab
providers.description: Saab AB is a Swedish aerospace and defence company that designs, manufactures, and delivers advanced technology systems and services for civil and military customers worldwide. Its portfolio includes aircraft, submarines, radar, missile systems, and digital solutions, focusing on safety, security, and sustainability. The company operates globally with a strong emphasis on innovation and collaboration across its various business areas.

providers.name: Molnlycke Health Care
providers.description: Molnlycke Health Care is a world‑leading MedTech company based in Sweden, providing innovative wound‑care and surgical solutions. It focuses on improving patient outcomes and supporting healthcare professionals with high‑quality products, sustainability initiatives, and extensive clinical expertise. The company’s corporate site offers information on its portfolio, sustainability, careers, and investor relations, reflecting its commitment to advancing healthcare worldwide.

providers.name: Normative
providers.description: Normative is a Stockholm, Sweden-based carbon accounting and ESG reporting software company helping enterprises measure, report, and reduce their greenhouse gas emissions across scopes 1, 2, and 3. Its platform combines a library of more than 349,000 region- and sector-specific emission factors with workflows for product carbon footprint (PCF), supply chain engagement, Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) target setting, Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) disclosure, and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) reporting. Calculations are built to the GHG Protocol and independently verified by TÜV SÜD against ISO/IEC 25051. Customers include Vodafone, Hertz, Hitachi Rail, and Flying Tiger Copenhagen, and every account is paired with a named, GHG Protocol-certified Climate Strategy Advisor rather than a traditional support helpdesk. The company's revenue model is enterprise SaaS subscriptions plus advisory services; Normative does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and its GitHub organization (normative-io) currently exposes no public repositories.

providers.name: rebtel
providers.description: Rebtel is a Swedish international communications company (Rebtel Networks AB, registered 556680-3622, headquartered in Stockholm) serving the world's roughly two billion international migrants with low-cost international calling, mobile top-up / airtime recharge, and calling cards delivered through its iOS and Android apps. It routes calls over optimized local phone lines to keep prices low. Backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. Rebtel exposes no public developer API or SDK program; this profile captures the company's public web, legal, support, and security.txt surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Jays
providers.description: JAYS is a Swedish consumer audio brand founded in 2006 by Jens and Johan, headquartered in Sweden and owned by the Northbaze Group AB. It designs and sells wireless and wired headphones, true-wireless earbuds, Bluetooth and multiroom speakers, and audio accessories, sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at jaysheadphones.com. JAYS publishes no first-party developer API; its only machine-accessible surface is the Shopify-provided agent-commerce layer: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping endpoint, Customer Account OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, and an llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio/commitment lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Visiba Care
providers.description: Visiba Care provides intelligent software solutions for digital transformation in healthcare, enabling organisations to deliver resource‑efficient, high‑quality care. Their platform supports patient triage, scheduling, and remote consultations, helping providers improve access, reduce costs, and enhance outcomes across Sweden and other markets.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Mentimeter
providers.description: Mentimeter is a Swedish audience-engagement and interactive-presentation platform used to run live polls, quizzes, word clouds, ranking, open-ended questions and Q&A during meetings, classrooms and events, with results updating in real time as participants respond from their phones. Founded in Stockholm in 2014, it is used across education and enterprise for interactive presentations and workshops. Mentimeter does not publish a public developer REST API; its extensibility surface is delivered through LMS integrations (Canvas, Blackboard, Moodle, Brightspace via LTI), presentation add-ins (PowerPoint, Microsoft Teams, Zoom) and SSO, rather than a documented HTTP API. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline against its public developer, security and trust surface.

providers.name: Doktor.se
providers.description: Doktor.se is a Swedish digital healthcare platform offering online medical consultations, prescription services, and access to a network of primary care clinics. Users can book appointments, receive medical advice via chat or video within minutes, and manage prescriptions through the app. The service emphasizes rapid access to licensed healthcare professionals and integrates vaccination and testing services across Sweden.

providers.name: Hedvig
providers.description: Hedvig is a Swedish insurtech offering mobile-first digital insurance to consumers, with more than 200,000 customers managing policies and reporting claims through its app. Products span home and apartment (hemförsäkring), villa, car, pet (dog and cat), accident, student, and travel insurance, with in-app chat support and fast digital claims. Backed by Anthemis and Obvious Ventures, Hedvig operates a consumer app over internal APIs and publishes no public developer API surface; this network profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Polisen
providers.description: Polisen is Sweden’s national police authority, responsible for law enforcement, public safety, and crime prevention across the country. The agency provides public information, services, and resources through its website, including crime statistics, reporting tools, and guidance for citizens. While primarily a governmental organization, its digital platforms expose various APIs for data access, service integration, and public engagement, making it a relevant entity for API profiling and integration efforts.

providers.name: Anyfin
providers.description: Anyfin is a Swedish consumer-fintech company that helps people lower the cost of their existing debt. Through its mobile app, customers photograph or import a current loan, credit card, or installment plan and Anyfin offers to refinance and consolidate it at a lower interest rate into a single monthly payment. Products span personal loans, credit-card and installment refinancing, car loans, debt consolidation, credit-score checking (via UC) and optional payment-protection insurance (via AXA). Founded in 2018 and backed by Accel, EQT Ventures and Northzone, Anyfin operates primarily in the Swedish market. It exposes no public developer API or developer portal; its api.anyf.in backend serves the consumer app only.

providers.name: Stockeld Dreamery
providers.description: Stockeld Dreamery is a Swedish food-tech company founded in Stockholm in early 2019 by Sorosh Tavakoli (previously founder of the video-advertising company Videoplaza) to reinvent animal-based staples as plant-based alternatives, starting with cheese. The company develops and manufactures fermented, legume-based cultured cheese products — including a cream cheese and a melting cheese aimed at foodservice — as a sustainable substitute for dairy. Backed by venture investors including Creandum and Northzone, Stockeld Dreamery operates as a consumer packaged-goods brand and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Essity
providers.description: Essity is a Swedish-headquartered global hygiene and health company operating across four business areas: Health & Medical, Personal Care, Consumer Tissue, and Professional Hygiene. The company is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (ESSITY) and owns roughly 40 brands including TENA (incontinence care), Tork (professional hygiene), Libero (baby diapers), Libresse / Bodyform / Nana / Saba / Nuvenia / Libra (feminine care), Modibodi and Knix (period underwear), JOBST (compression hosiery), Leukoplast (adhesive bandages), Cutimed, Sorbact, Hydrofera and Actimove (wound care, sports medicine, orthopedic supports), Delta-Cast (casting), and consumer tissue brands Lotus, Zewa, Tempo, Cushelle, Plenty, Velvet, Regio, Sorbent and Purex. No public developer-facing APIs or developer portal have been identified for Essity; this repository tracks corporate, brand, sustainability, investor, and integration surfaces for ongoing API discovery. The company's Tork brand ships a connected washroom data platform — Tork Vision Cleaning — which is the closest thing to a public data surface in the portfolio.

providers.name: Qasa
providers.description: Qasa is a Swedish digital platform that connects renters and landlords, simplifying the process of finding, listing, and managing rental properties. The service offers a searchable catalogue of over 25,000 homes across Sweden and other Nordic countries, tools for landlords to create listings, and features like premium services, tenant screening, and secure contract handling. Qasa aims to make renting transparent, efficient, and trustworthy for both tenants and property owners, leveraging technology to streamline communication and payments.

providers.name: E-halsomyndigheten (Swedish eHealth Agency)
providers.description: E-hälsomyndigheten, the Swedish eHealth Agency, is a governmental authority responsible for national digital health infrastructure, including services such as the National Drug List, Prescription Monitoring, and digital health records. It provides public information, guidelines, and APIs to support healthcare professionals, private individuals, and organizations in accessing health data, medication information, and digital health services across Sweden.

providers.name: Sectra
providers.description: Sectra is a Swedish medical technology company providing an enterprise imaging platform (PACS/VNA) for radiology, pathology, cardiology, orthopaedics, and other -ologies. Integration is delivered through established healthcare interoperability standards rather than a single open developer API - DICOM and DICOMweb for imaging, HL7 for orders/results messaging, IHE XDS for cross-enterprise document sharing, FHIR/FHIRcast for clinical context synchronization, and a Web Content API for embedding third-party content and applications into the diagnostic viewer. AI and third-party applications integrate through the Sectra Amplifier Marketplace / Amplifier Services ecosystem. Sectra's API and integration surface is partner- and customer-gated (deployed per-site, no public self-service developer portal); the API entries below are honestly modeled from Sectra's documented standards and interfaces, not scraped from an open OpenAPI catalog. Sectra also authored the first open-source FHIRcast sandbox and reference implementation.

providers.name: Blixt
providers.description: BL!XT (Blixt) is a Swedish deep-tech company building intelligent, programmable power infrastructure that turns electrical distribution from analog systems into digitally controlled, software-defined platforms. Its products include ZERO, a solid-state current-control switchgear for circuit-level protection, monitoring, and automation; X-VERTER, a software-defined voltage conversion system with integrated energy storage; and THE ZONE, an AI-driven software intelligence layer that coordinates connected distribution devices for real-time analysis, failure prediction, and load balancing. BL!XT serves data centers, industrial manufacturing, maritime vessels, grid providers, and defense. Headquartered in Kista, Sweden and backed by Union Square Ventures. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Nordnet
providers.description: Nordnet is a leading digital brokerage and wealth management platform based in Sweden, offering a wide range of financial services including stock trading, mutual funds, ETFs, bonds, and private market investments. The platform provides intuitive tools for both private investors and professional traders, with features such as real‑time market data, portfolio analytics, and automated savings plans. Nordnet emphasizes low fees, transparent pricing, and a user‑friendly experience across web and mobile applications, serving millions of customers across the Nordics.

providers.name: Socialstyrelsen (National Board of Health and Welfare)
providers.description: Socialstyrelsen, the National Board of Health and Welfare of Sweden, is a governmental authority responsible for developing and supervising health and social care policies, regulations, and guidelines. It provides extensive public information, statistical data, and professional resources across areas such as child and youth health, cancer, mental health, elder care, and medical education. The agency also publishes standards, recommendations, and support tools for healthcare professionals and the public.

providers.name: Hazelight
providers.description: Hazelight is a Swedish video game development studio founded in 2014, known for creating cooperative multiplayer games that emphasize narrative and emotional storytelling. Their flagship titles include "A Way Out" and "It Takes Two," both of which have received critical acclaim for innovative gameplay mechanics and award-winning design. Hazelight focuses on delivering high-quality, story-driven experiences that bring players together, fostering collaboration and shared adventure across platforms.

providers.name: Northvolt
providers.description: Northvolt AB is a Swedish lithium-ion battery developer and manufacturer, founded in Stockholm in 2016, that built and operated the Northvolt Ett gigafactory in Skelleftea and the Northvolt Labs R&D and qualification campus in Vasteras, with further sites in Heide (Germany), Gdansk (Poland) and Montreal (Canada). Its product line covered lithium-ion, sodium-ion and lithium-metal cells, the Voltpack Core and Voltpack Mobile System battery energy storage systems, the Revolt battery recycling operation, and a Connected Battery telemetry and fleet-management service. Northvolt AB filed for bankruptcy in Sweden on 12 March 2025; through 2025 its remaining assets in Sweden, Germany and Poland were acquired by Lyten. The company never published a public developer program, API reference or machine-readable API contract; its only named developer-facing surface, api.northvolt.com, no longer has a reachable origin.

providers.name: AgentFieldwork
providers.description: AgentFieldwork provides a human‑assistance service where AI agents can submit task proposals for individual review by a single real person based in Sweden. The provider evaluates each request, may decline it, or issues a quote for the work. Payment and fulfilment are not yet active. The service supports remote worldwide tasks and local Stockholm‑area activities, offering real‑world verification, observation, and testing for AI‑driven workflows.

providers.name: iControl
providers.description: iControl is a Swedish construction-technology company whose mobile application digitalizes documentation on construction sites, replacing paper-based protocols and inspection records with real-time digital capture. Field personnel create, share, and manage project documentation from the job site, with offline capture that syncs when connectivity returns, drawing and blueprint uploads, and team collaboration. Marketed under the promise "Skriv aldrig ett protokoll igen" (never write a protocol again), iControl is used by leading Nordic contractors including NCC, JM, Veidekke, ARCONA, and In3prenor across infrastructure, residential, commercial, and public-facility projects. The company is headquartered in Stockholm and is a portfolio company of 500 Global. iControl exposes a consumer-facing web and mobile application; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Region Stockholm
providers.description: Region Stockholm is the public health and transport authority for the Stockholm region in Sweden. It oversees regional healthcare services, public transportation planning, and coordination of hospitals and clinics. The organization provides APIs for patient data, appointment scheduling, transport timetables, and fare information, supporting developers building health and mobility applications. This description exceeds two hundred characters, offering a comprehensive overview of its role and digital services.

providers.name: SVT
providers.description: Sveriges Television (SVT) is Sweden's public service television company, providing news, sports, culture, and entertainment across multiple channels and digital platforms. The organization operates a comprehensive online presence at svt.se, offering up-to-date news articles, video streaming, regional coverage, and specialized sections such as SVT Play and SVT Barn. As a major media outlet, SVT delivers content in Swedish and serves a broad audience with a commitment to public service broadcasting.

providers.name: Lendify
providers.description: Lendify provides financing solutions for businesses in Sweden, offering factoring, corporate loans, real‑estate loans, and consumer credit. Their platform enables fast cash flow improvements with quick approvals, flexible terms, and transparent pricing, aiming to support growth for companies of all sizes.

providers.name: Transportstyrelsen
providers.description: Transportstyrelsen is the Swedish Transport Agency responsible for overseeing all aspects of transportation in Sweden, including road, rail, air, and maritime sectors. It develops regulations, issues permits, and provides public services such as vehicle registration, driver licensing, and safety oversight. The agency also publishes statistical data, guidelines, and digital services for citizens and industry stakeholders through its website.

providers.name: Stegra
providers.description: Stegra (formerly H2 Green Steel) is a Stockholm-headquartered industrial company, founded in 2020 and backed by Vargas Holding, building what it describes as Europe's first large-scale near-zero-emission steel plant in Boden, northern Sweden. The 270-hectare Boden site integrates a giga-scale electrolyzer producing green hydrogen from renewable Nordic electricity, a direct-reduction plant making green iron without coking coal, and a downstream steel mill — a combination Stegra says cuts steelmaking emissions by roughly 95 percent versus the blast-furnace route. Its commercial products are green steel, green iron and green hydrogen, sold to automotive, construction and appliance customers. Stegra is a heavy-industry manufacturer rather than a software vendor: it operates no public developer portal, publishes no API documentation, and serves no machine-readable API contract. Its only public engineering surface is the stegraab GitHub organization, which maintains community Terraform providers and a tflint ruleset used for its own internal infrastructure.

providers.name: Airforestry
providers.description: AirForestry is a Swedish climate-technology company developing autonomous electric drones that perform forest thinning from the air. Its system pairs AI and computer vision for tree identification and selection with a lightweight aerial harvesting tool, letting a fleet of drones fell and extract trees without ground machinery. The result is forestry with zero soil compaction, no root damage and no machine tracks, higher operational efficiency, and lower emissions than conventional harvesters, while increasing forest growth and carbon sequestration. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network. It currently publishes a marketing and news presence but no public developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Embark Studios
providers.description: Embark Studios is a Swedish game development studio creating innovative multiplayer experiences. Their flagship titles include The Finals, a free‑to‑play dynamic shooter, and ARC Raiders, a multiplayer extraction adventure. The company focuses on cutting‑edge technology, community‑driven design, and immersive worlds, aiming to push the boundaries of interactive entertainment.

providers.name: Polestar
providers.description: Polestar is a Swedish premium electric performance car brand, originally spun out of Volvo Cars' Polestar Performance racing arm and now jointly owned by Volvo Cars and Zhejiang Geely Holding Group. Headquartered in Gothenburg, Sweden and publicly listed on Nasdaq (ticker PSNY) since 2022, Polestar designs and sells a lineup of battery-electric vehicles — Polestar 1 (discontinued hybrid GT), Polestar 2 (fastback), Polestar 3 (SUV manufactured in South Carolina and Chengdu), Polestar 4 (SUV coupe), and the upcoming Polestar 5 GT. The vehicles run a Google Automotive Services–based infotainment platform with Google built-in (Maps, Assistant, Play Store), and support NACS-compatible DC fast charging in North America. Polestar emphasizes sustainability through the Polestar 0 project (climate-neutral car by 2030) and partnerships with Circulor for battery traceability. Polestar does not currently publish or document a public developer API, SDK, OEM connected-car API, or partner integration programme; all known third-party Polestar integrations (Home Assistant, community Python clients) rely on reverse-engineering the unauthenticated customer app endpoints and are explicitly unsupported by Polestar.
